Delivery Hero treats the pre-August 2021 model as a probable risk and the post-August 2021 model as a contingency.

- For the model operated by Glovo Spain until August 2021, the rider risk is considered more likely than not, so appropriate provisions are recognized in the Consolidated Financial Statements (Strategic Risks, passage [1]).
- During 2024, Glovo had to provide bank guarantees to Spanish courts to secure payment of the liabilities claimed by Spanish authorities for that pre-August 2021 model (Strategic Risks, passages [2] and [5]).
- For the model in place since August 2021, the risk is deemed possible but not probable, so it is disclosed as a contingent liability of €440 to 770 million in the notes, with no provision recognized, since court reclassification was assessed as not probable (Strategic Risks [1], Auditor's Report [3], Contingencies [4]).
- In December 2024, Glovo's management decided to progressively move to an employment-based model in Spain to avoid further legal uncertainties regarding the model in place since August 2021, while Glovo will defend the self-employed status through all available instances and continue cooperating with the Spanish authorities (Strategic Risks, passage [5]).

Zalando - end of 2022: EUR 304.3m committed to further invest in fulfilment centres
Zalando - end of 2024: 59.5m EUR committed to further invest in fulfilment centres

The commitment fell by 244.8m EUR (304.3m − 59.5m), from EUR 304.3m at the end of 2022 to 59.5m EUR at the end of 2024.
Approximately 850,000 riders delivered at least one order for Delivery Hero in 2024.

Zalando changed Zalando Plus in 2024 from a paid membership to a free-to-join model with a points-based system rewarding engagement (purchases, newsletter subscriptions), unlocking four benefit levels; it was tested in Spain, expanded to France and Austria, and will roll out to more markets in 2025. The report also mentions increased accruals at the beginning of 2025 for reimbursing Zalando Plus subscription fees to customers, included in "others" within other current non-financial liabilities (which rose to 377.4m EUR, with "thereof others" at 25.0m EUR).

Vodafone Turkey - 2G licence extension: €120 million for a six-year extension until 30 April 2029 (excluding 18% VAT), paid in advance with a capital injection.
Turkcell - 2G licence extension: EUR 120 million (plus EUR 21.6 million of value-added taxes), paid in installments — an initial payment of EUR 81.6 million (TRY 1.7 billion) in 2023, approximately EUR 31.1 million (TRY 1.1 billion) in April 2024, with the remainder due within a year.

Both agreed to the same €120 million fee, but Vodafone Turkey paid it in advance via a capital injection, while Turkcell paid in installments in Turkish Lira over 2023–2025.
